_meta.description: Lawmaker term, committee, and power-status history. Used by earmark_detector to assess whether a known earmark's sponsoring lawmakers are still in power.
_meta.scope: Hand-curated for known earmark-relevant lawmakers (initially: those associated with IONQ AFRL Quantum, Qubitekk, UMD adds). Extend by adding more entries.

lawmakers.name: Ben Cardin
lawmakers.lost_power_reason: Did not seek re-election; term ended at start of 119th Congress
lawmakers._note: Senior Maryland Democrat; long-time advocate for UMD-aligned research earmarks including quantum networking via AFRL collaboration with University of Maryland (College Park, MD).

lawmakers.name: Chris Van Hollen

key_committees.name: Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Financial Services and General Government
key_committees._note: Lost gavel in 119th Congress as Republicans took majority

lawmakers._note: Maryland Senator; Senate Appropriations Defense Subcommittee member. Aligned with UMD/quantum networking interests. Still in office but in minority as of 119th Congress.

lawmakers.name: Jamie Raskin
lawmakers.lost_power_reason: House majority flipped to Republicans in 118th Congress
lawmakers._note: Maryland congressman; represents College Park (UMD); supportive of UMD quantum earmarks. Currently in minority.

lawmakers.name: Steny Hoyer
lawmakers.lost_power_reason: Stepped down from House Majority Leader; lost gavel; House minority since 118th Congress
lawmakers._note: Long-serving Maryland Democrat; House Appropriations Defense Subcommittee member; central to UMD-aligned defense research earmarks. Lost leadership in 118th and remains in minority.

lawmakers.name: Dianne Feinstein
lawmakers._note: California senator; Senate Appropriations Defense Subcommittee senior member. Aligned with Qubitekk (San Diego, CA) earmark advocacy; her death and successor (Butler/Schiff) transition reduced earmark continuity for CA-based defense quantum work.

lawmakers.name: Alex Padilla
lawmakers._note: California senator; succeeded into Senate Appropriations Defense Subcommittee role. In minority as of 119th Congress.

lawmakers.name: Jon Tester

key_committees.name: Senate Appropriations Defense Subcommittee
key_committees._note: Senate Approps Defense Subcommittee Chair during peak IONQ earmark period

lawmakers.lost_power_reason: Lost re-election November 2024 to Tim Sheehy (R-MT)
lawmakers._note: Montana senator; Senate Appropriations Defense Subcommittee Chair / Ranking. The Senate Defense Approps Chair during 2021-2023 has significant earmark influence. Loss of seat in 2024 election is a canonical 'sponsor lost power' transition.
